request: how do you rearrange v = u + at to find t?

beats.intent: A bar for v = 20 above two bars, u = 5 and at = 15, that fill the same length
beats.narration: Take v equals u plus a t, with v twenty, u five and a three. The whole of v is u and a t laid end to end.
beats.code:
stage.title("Rearranging v = u + at")
k = 0.3
x0 = -6
vbar = Rectangle(width=20 * k, height=0.6, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([x0 + 10 * k, 1.2, 0])
ubar = Rectangle(width=5 * k, height=0.6, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([x0 + 2.5 * k, 0.2, 0])
atbar = Rectangle(width=15 * k, height=0.6, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([x0 + 12.5 * k, 0.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(vbar))
stage.play(FadeIn(ubar), FadeIn(atbar))
stage.add(vbar, ubar, atbar)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("v = 20", font_size=26).move_to(vbar)), FadeIn(Text("u = 5", font_size=24).move_to(ubar)), FadeIn(Text("at", font_size=26).move_to(atbar)))

beats.intent: The u part greyed out: what's left, v − u = 15, is at
beats.narration: Take u away from both: v minus u is what's left, fifteen, and that is a t.
beats.code:
stage.play(ubar.animate.set_fill(GREY_D, opacity=0.4).set_stroke(GREY_D))
stage.label(atbar, "v − u = 15", direction=DOWN, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: The at bar cut into t pieces of length a = 3: five pieces
beats.narration: a t means t lots of a. Cut fifteen into pieces of three: there are five, so t is five.
beats.code:
pieces = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=3 * k, height=0.6, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([x0 + 12.5 * k, -1.4, 0])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(p) for p in pieces], lag_ratio=0.2))
stage.add(pieces)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text("3", font_size=22).move_to(p)) for p in pieces])
stage.label(pieces, "15 ÷ 3 = 5 pieces", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The bars beside v = u + at, v − u = at, t = (v − u)/a
beats.narration: In symbols: subtract u from both sides, then divide both sides by a. t is v minus u, over a.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"v = u + at", r"v - u = at", r"t = \frac{v - u}{a}")

request: why are two triangles with the same three sides always identical?

beats.narration: Take three sticks: three, four and five units long.
beats.code:
stage.title("Same three sides")
k = 0.6
sticks = VGroup(Line(ORIGIN, 3 * k * RIGHT, color=BLUE), Line(ORIGIN, 4 * k * RIGHT, color=GREEN), Line(ORIGIN, 5 * k * RIGHT, color=ORANGE)).set_stroke(width=8).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([-4, 1.2, 0])
stage.play(Create(sticks))
stage.add(sticks)
nums = VGroup(*[Text(t, font_size=24).next_to(s, RIGHT) for s, t in zip(sticks, ("3", "4", "5"))])
stage.play(FadeIn(nums))
stage.add(nums)

beats.intent: The sticks joined end to end into a triangle
beats.narration: Join them end to end. Once the corners are fixed, the triangle can't wobble: those three lengths allow only one shape.
beats.code:
P = np.array([-5.5, -2.3, 0])
tri1 = Polygon(P, P + 4 * k * RIGHT, P + 3 * k * UP, color=WHITE)
sides1 = VGroup(Line(P, P + 4 * k * RIGHT, color=GREEN), Line(P + 4 * k * RIGHT, P + 3 * k * UP, color=ORANGE), Line(P + 3 * k * UP, P, color=BLUE)).set_stroke(width=8)
stage.play(Transform(sticks, sides1), FadeOut(nums), run_time=1.5)
stage.add(sticks)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("4", font_size=24).next_to(sides1[0], DOWN)), FadeIn(Text("5", font_size=24).move_to(sides1[1].get_center() + 0.3 * UR)), FadeIn(Text("3", font_size=24).next_to(sides1[2], LEFT)))

beats.intent: A second triangle from the same lengths, turned and flipped elsewhere, slid onto the first: a perfect fit
beats.narration: Build another from the same three lengths, any way round you like. Turn it and slide it, and it lands exactly on the first.
beats.code:
sides2 = sides1.copy().set_stroke(YELLOW, width=3).rotate(2.2).flip(UP).move_to([-0.5, 0.4, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(sides2))
stage.add(sides2)
stage.play(sides2.animate.flip(UP).rotate(-2.2).move_to(sides1), run_time=2)
stage.add(sides2)
stage.label(sides1, "exactly the same", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The triangle with its three sides marked equal: SSS means congruent
beats.narration: So two triangles with the same three sides are congruent: same shape, same size. Mathematicians call this rule S S S.

request: how do you factorise x² + 5x + 6 with algebra tiles?

beats.intent: An x² tile, five x tiles and six unit tiles laid out separately
beats.narration: x squared plus five x plus six as tiles: one big square, five long strips, six little squares.
beats.code:
stage.title("Factorising with tiles")
X, U = 1.6, 0.4
tl = np.array([-5.0, 1.6, 0])
big = Square(X, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([-5.2, 0.8, 0])
strips = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=U, height=X, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15).move_to([-2.4, 0.8, 0])
units = VGroup(*[Square(U, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(6)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15).move_to([-3.6, -1.4, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(big), FadeIn(strips), FadeIn(units))
stage.add(big, strips, units)
stage.label(big, "x²", direction=UP, color=BLUE)
stage.label(strips, "5x", direction=UP, color=GREEN)
stage.label(units, "6", direction=DOWN, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: The tiles fitted into one rectangle: x² top left, three strips on its right, two below, six units in the corner
beats.narration: Fit them together into a rectangle: three strips down the side, two along the bottom, and the six little squares fill the corner exactly.
beats.code:
stage.clear(keep=(big, strips, units))
moves = [big.animate.move_to(tl + np.array([X / 2, -X / 2, 0]))]
moves += [strips[i].animate.move_to(tl + np.array([X + U / 2 + U * i, -X / 2, 0])) for i in range(3)]
moves += [strips[3 + j].animate.rotate(PI / 2).move_to(tl + np.array([X / 2, -X - U / 2 - U * j, 0])) for j in range(2)]
moves += [units[3 * j + i].animate.move_to(tl + np.array([X + U / 2 + U * i, -X - U / 2 - U * j, 0])) for j in range(2) for i in range(3)]
stage.play(*moves, run_time=2)
stage.add(big, strips, units)

beats.intent: The rectangle's sides labelled x + 3 across and x + 2 down
beats.narration: The rectangle is x plus three wide and x plus two tall.
beats.code:
top = Line(tl, tl + (X + 3 * U) * RIGHT)
left = Line(tl, tl + (X + 2 * U) * DOWN)
stage.label(top, "x + 3", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(left, "x + 2", direction=LEFT, color=YELLOW)

beats.narration: Its area is the same tiles, so x squared plus five x plus six equals x plus two times x plus three.

request: how do you work out 156 ÷ 12 by chunking?

beats.narration: One hundred and fifty six divided by twelve: how many twelves fit into one hundred and fifty six?
beats.code:
stage.title("156 ÷ 12 by chunking")
k = 0.03
x0 = -6
bar = Rectangle(width=156 * k, height=0.7, color=WHITE).move_to([x0 + 78 * k, 0.6, 0])
stage.play(Create(bar))
stage.add(bar)
stage.label(bar, "156", direction=UP)

beats.intent: A chunk of ten twelves, 120, shaded; 36 left
beats.narration: Take a big easy chunk: ten twelves is a hundred and twenty. That leaves thirty six.
beats.code:
c1 = Rectangle(width=120 * k, height=0.7, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([x0 + 60 * k, 0.6, 0])
stage.play(GrowFromEdge(c1, LEFT))
stage.add(c1)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("10 × 12 = 120", font_size=24).move_to(c1)))
stage.label(c1, "36 left", direction=DOWN + RIGHT, color=GREY_B)

beats.intent: A chunk of three twelves, 36, filling the rest
beats.narration: Three twelves is thirty six, which uses up the rest exactly.
beats.code:
c2 = Rectangle(width=36 * k, height=0.7, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([x0 + 138 * k, 0.6, 0])
stage.play(GrowFromEdge(c2, LEFT))
stage.add(c2)
stage.label(c2, "3 × 12 = 36", direction=UP, color=ORANGE)

beats.narration: Ten twelves and three twelves: thirteen twelves altogether. One hundred and fifty six divided by twelve is thirteen.
